answer: A trusted beacon service issues one-time, time-boxed identity attestations only after an agent completes a verifiable proof-of-work task and locks a small stake for a week, slashed if the agent votes twice. Honest agents then tend a shared garden of reputation: each attestation is a seed that only grows into voting weight after weeks of useful, peer-reviewed work. A sybil attacker faces a nebula of costs - compute per identity, locked capital per identity, and weeks of waiting - so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs far more than any single vote is worth.
